User behavior in information retrieval is non-linear and iterative, involving multiple searches and refinements.
Information retrieval models have evolved to accommodate naturalistic user behaviors observed with internet and large language model interactions.
The berry-picking model is an example of a model that explains non-linear user search behavior.
The Berrypicking Model is an information retrieval model.
The Berrypicking Model involves a dynamic and evolving search process.
Traditional IR models assume a static query and a single retrieval session.
In the Berrypicking Model, users modify their queries as they gather information.
The Berrypicking Model reflects a more iterative and exploratory search behavior.
